lessons: run_go_grade hardcodes run_seq=0, so later runs replay earlier results and the evidence is fabricated. Compute run_seq as the count of prior review_baseline signals in the journal, using one helper shared with run(). Test: run() first, then run_go_grade makes all 51 fresh model calls.

The cap must be strict: charged spend can never exceed USD 5.00. Before each call, refuse unless the remaining headroom covers a per-call bound, such as the largest cost seen so far. Rewrite the cap test so the refused call is never issued and recorded spend is <= 5.00.

The Unscored cap message must be true. Do not say 'no further model call was made' if a call already crossed the cap. After the pre-call reservation fix, the message should name the headroom and the per-call bound that refused the call.

Keep the parts review accepted: closed ReviewBaselineReport, KNOWN_ARTIFACTS registration, and the record_go operator path. Change only the run_seq and cap logic and their tests, and keep the diff inside the fence.
Before reporting ok, map each acceptance criterion and each review finding to a specific test assertion. The run record claimed ok at 25m of a 75m budget while two correctness defects remained.
reason: Review found two concrete, fixable defects, and each came with a paved road: hardcoded run_seq=0 causes replay/fabricated evidence, and the post-hoc cap check allows overflow. Registration, report validation and the GO path passed review, so the same capability can fix this.
